_doc: SURFACE PARITY REGISTRY. This contract exists because zzop shipped the same bug class more than once: the facade computed a field (configWarnings; git-derived health/recommendations/critical; the run-level, join-scoped MultiAnalyzeOutput::warnings channel, e.g. the parallel-implementation tripwire) but the delivery surface silently dropped it. Every top-level field of AnalyzeOutputView and MultiAnalyzeOutputView (crates/facade/src/output.rs) must get exactly one row below, naming what the delivery surface — the MCP analyze_repo/cross_repo reply, which is the SAME shaped summary the `zzop analyze`/`zzop cross` CLI subcommands print (that is the `zzop` binary, packages/cli-bin; `zzop-mcp` takes NO analysis subcommands at all — bare or `mcp` serves stdio and `version`/`help` are the only other forms) — does with it: 'carry' (forwarded unconditionally), 'carry-conditional' (forwarded only in some shaped/capped/gated form, or only when a precondition holds), or 'omit' (never surfaced by the reply). Every 'omit'/'carry-conditional' row MUST carry a non-empty 'note' explaining why and where the data IS available — which, for anything the shaped reply drops, is either the raw zzop-facade output you get by embedding the engine directly or one of the CLI-only lanes in '_cliOnlyLanes' below (since 2026-07-26 `zzop facts` emits the full CommonIr and the whole cross-layer join, so 'available ONLY via a direct embedding' is no longer true of either — check the row's own note). HISTORICAL NOTE: this registry briefly tracked two JS-CLI render surfaces (a pretty terminal render backed by lib/format.js and a markdown report backed by lib/report.js) across the npm distribution's 2026-07-20 removal-then-restoration; @zzop/cli is now a zero-logic shim that spawns the native `zzop` binary with no render logic of its own, so those two columns are dropped again and only the reply lane remains. SCANNED DELIVERY LANE — what an 'omit' row's note means when it says a field is 'never referenced': the meta-test's haystack is every non-test .rs file under THREE directories, crates/summary/src AND packages/mcp/src AND packages/cli-bin/src (canonical list: mcp_lane_dirs() in crates/engine/tests/rule_contracts/surface_parity.rs), minus the `_cliOnlyLanes` implementations declared below. The notes below say 'the scanned delivery lane' and mean all three — never crates/summary/src alone, which would understate the set and let a note read true while packages/mcp/src referenced the field. WORKFLOW FOR FUTURE BATCH AGENTS: adding a field to AnalyzeOutputView or MultiAnalyzeOutputView? Add this registry's row for it IN THE SAME COMMIT — crates/engine/tests/rule_contracts/surface_parity.rs's completeness test fails the build otherwise, by design. This file documents TODAY's truth, not an aspiration: a row reflects what the code actually does, not what it should eventually do.

_cliOnlyLanes._doc: Delivery lanes that exist ONLY on the `zzop` CLI, with the reason each has no MCP tool twin, and the .rs files that implement each one's PROJECTION. What `sources` means, precisely, because the subtraction below depends on it: the projection implementation under crates/summary/** — NOT the argv entry points that route to it (packages/cli-bin/src/main.rs and its cli/ module). Those files are deliberately NOT declared, and must not be: they also dispatch lanes that are NOT CLI-only (`analyze`, `cross`, `endpoint`), so subtracting them wholesale would blind the haystack to a real MCP-lane leak in exactly the files where argv meets the shared handlers. The consequence of leaving them in is FAIL-SAFE, which is why it is the right side to err on: if an argv file ever emits an `omit` field's key literal, the guard reads it as an MCP-lane leak and goes RED (a false red someone must then explain), never green. As of 2026-07-26 neither file spells any registry field name as a JSON key literal outside a comment, so nothing is failing today. The PROSE here is documentation (the meta-test's SURFACES list in crates/engine/tests/rule_contracts/surface_parity.rs covers `mcpAnalyzeReply` alone) — recorded so a future batch does not 'restore parity' by adding a twin without re-reading why there isn't one. The `sources` arrays, however, ARE machine-read (since 2026-07-26): that meta-test's carry/omit check subtracts exactly those files from the MCP lane it scans, so this block is what defines the boundary between 'a CLI-only lane deliberately emits this' and 'the MCP reply leaks it'. Consequences, both deliberate: a lane that ships without declaring its sources leaves them inside the MCP lane and fails the build the moment it emits an `omit` field (declare the lane, do not rename the key around the guard); and a declared path that no longer resolves is a hard failure, so a moved lane source must update this file in the same commit. The subtraction applies to `carry` rows too — a CLI-only emission must never be what keeps a `carry` row green after the MCP reply stopped forwarding it. NOTE for the `zzop manifest` and `zzop facts` rows below: because both read fields the shaped reply drops, an `omit` row's note can no longer say 'available ONLY via a direct zzop-facade embedding' without qualification — see the `ir` row.

zzop manifest.emits: Identity rows only — provides {kind,key,source}, edges {kind,key,from,to}, buckets {bucket,kind,key,source} — sorted, deduped, UNCAPPED, plus a `tool` fingerprint (zzop_facade::version_string) and per-source {joinContributionZero, degraded}. No file, no line, no root path, no findings.
zzop manifest.noMcpTwinBecause: (1) The manifest is deliberately UNCAPPED, and every MCP reply this repo ships is cap-governed (the token-bomb guard crates/summary/src/output exists for); putting it on that wire would force a choice between breaking that doctrine and capping the one artifact whose whole reason for existing is that the caps make two capped summaries un-diffable above them. (2) The workflow is file-shaped, not conversation-shaped: a manifest earns its keep by being COMMITTED and compared by a later run (the scripts/max-file-lines-baseline.txt model). (3) An agent that wants it can shell out to the same binary — the analysis path is identical.

reads: two `zzop manifest` outputs — no engine, no filesystem beyond the two files
zzop diff.emits: transitions (a key's bucket placement changed — the ranked signal), sources {added, removed, coverageDropped}, and per-relation added/removed for provides/edges/buckets, with `blindnessSuspect` on any removal attributable to a source that lost coverage.
zzop diff.noMcpTwinBecause: It consumes manifests; without a `manifest` twin an agent could not produce its own inputs, so a diff-only tool would be half a surface. Ships with `manifest` or not at all.

reads: trees[].output.gitWindow (presence only — the gate on whether git collection ran)
trees[].output.nodes[].{path,changeCount,churn,authorCount,lastModified} (the dep domain's history axes, read only when that gate says git ran)
trees[].output.scores (presence only — the numbers are deliberately NOT drawn)
zzop graph.emits: TWO FORMATS, selected by `--format`, because its consumer is a renderer rather than a parser. (A) `--format mermaid` (DEFAULT, every domain) — MERMAID TEXT, the one zzop product that is not a JSON document. (B) `--format cosmograph-nodes|cosmograph-links` (`--domain dep` ONLY, a usage error elsewhere) — NDJSON tables for an interactive viewer, one record per line, emitted UNCAPPED: `--top` is refused rather than ignored, because capping exists to keep a DRAWN picture readable and a viewer with zoom does that job itself. Measured on zzop's own tree, mermaid draws 40 of 1165 files where this lane emits all 1165 and all 2154 edges (re-measured 2026-08-01; the figure moves with the repo, so it is illustrative of the RATIO, not a pinned constant), which is the case dep.rs's module doc reserved when it said a large graph is where a different format stays live. Both formats read the SAME uncapped `dep::collect` pass, so they cannot become two answers about one repo. The nodes table carries the axes a viewer styles by; the links table carries `source`/`target`/`endpointsInCycle` — named for the ENDPOINT test it actually runs (both ends are members of some reported cycle), because the reported cycles are flattened into one member set, so a chord inside a cycle and an edge bridging two DIFFERENT cycles both score true without lying on a cycle themselves; the NODE column keeps the name `inCycle`, where claim and computation agree. Nine node columns are STRUCTURAL — `id`/`source`/`path`/`label`/`folder`/`fanIn`/`fanOut`/`degree`/`inCycle`, where `label` is a basename — derived from the graph itself, so every row has them. The rest are MEASURED and ride only when this run measured them: `loc` (from `ir.loc`) and, when `gitWindow` says git collection ran, `changeCount`/`churn`/`authorCount`/`lastModified` (from `nodes[]`). No flag adds or removes a column — a schema that changed per invocation is one no consumer could write against — so what varies is whether a ROW HAS a key. An unmeasured axis is OMITTED, never written as `0`: `churn: 0` would say 'never changed' in the same bytes as 'nobody looked', and a viewer colouring by it would draw the second as the first. That is also why the git axes are gated on `gitWindow` rather than read field-by-field: `nodes[]` is built unconditionally and its counters default to `0`, so on a git-off run every row on the wire carries a perfectly-formed `changeCount: 0`. NDJSON rather than CSV so `serde_json` owns quoting (a path containing a comma cannot silently shift columns). DISCLOSURE GOES TO STDERR for this format, never into the table: stdout is a parseable table and a `%%` census line would be a corrupt row, so the CLI prints the scope/total census on the other stream — and that census also reports how many emitted rows carried each MEASURED axis (`loc on N of M row(s), git history on N of M`), because omitting an unmeasured column is honest but silent: without the count, a reader whose viewer offers no colour-by-churn has nothing to read. A `flowchart LR` with one subgraph per analyzed source and one node per (sourceId, side, kind, key): rectangles for provides, stadiums for consumes, solid arrows for resolved edges, DOTTED arrows for the two non-authoritative relations (an ambiguous consume to each candidate provider, and an edge the linker flagged `lowConfidenceReason`). Each node's bucket rides its LABEL as well as its `classDef` class, so a viewer that drops styling still reads the verdict. SCOPED BY CONSTRUCTION: `--top` caps DRAWN RELATIONS per bucket (default 25, no upper bound — a file/pipe surface, not the capped wire; rows are deduped to distinct relations BEFORE the cap, because a node aggregates call sites and a row-based cap described a picture the reader was not looking at — measured on the OSS corpus, 60 `edges` rows are 4 relations) and `--scope <prefix>` keeps rows whose source id or a site path starts with the prefix; both are disclosed twice, in a `%%` per-bucket drawn/inScope/total-relations census that also publishes the call-site count each aggregates, AND as a visible note node, since a mermaid comment does not survive rendering. NOT emitted, and named in the document's own header rather than left to inference: `crossLayerFindings` (the drift/near-miss VERDICTS — findings ABOUT the join, not members of it; a finding has no node identity here and inventing one would be inventing facts the IR does not have), `hostRekeyCounts` (a counter, not an edge), the warnings/configWarnings/disclosure prose channels, and per-site file/line (nodes AGGREGATE call sites — `zzop facts`/`zzop cross`'s `distinctBucketKeyFirstSites` carry sites). An item with neither `key` nor `raw` is counted as an unlabelable remainder in the census, never guessed at.
zzop graph.noMcpTwinBecause: (1) A diagram is a terminal/file act — `zzop graph ./api ./web > join.mmd` then a renderer — the same file- and pipe-shaped lane `manifest` and `facts` argued for; an agent that wants the picture shells out to the same binary for identical bytes. (2) The shaped answers already exist on the MCP wire: `cross_repo` carries the same buckets as counts, keys and sites, which is what a PROGRAM reasons over, while a flowchart is for a human eye. A tool twin would put the same data on two surfaces under two different shaping rules — the exact drift class this registry exists to prevent. (3) Since the cosmograph format landed, this lane also emits an UNCAPPED table — 1165 nodes and 2154 edges on zzop's own tree — which is the same argument `manifest` and `facts` make, only now it applies to a lane whose reader is explicitly a HUMAN at a viewer rather than an agent in a conversation. Putting it on the cap-governed wire would force capping the one output whose reason for existing is that it is not capped.

zzop facts.emits: The whole post-assembly FACT SUBSTRATE, UNCAPPED and verbatim: `{tool, config, configWarnings, trees[{sourceId, coverage, warnings, commonIr}], crossLayer, warnings, disclosure}`. The consumer half of the custom-rule extension point — zzop emits what it knows and a user's own program decides what is a problem. It executes nothing (no process spawn) and ingests nothing (no findings channel back in). NOT emitted: zzop's own `findings`/`crossLayerFindings` (verdicts, not facts — a rule author computes their own, and carrying ours would put the same data on two surfaces under two different caps), and `AttributeStore` (the one post-assembly fact whose CONTAINER is not already a serialized wire shape; emitting it would freeze a NEW shape, which this repo's projection-contract bar gates behind a consuming rule existing first). KEY NAMING: the per-tree IR rides under `commonIr`, not `ir` — a design choice, and (since 2026-07-26) no longer a guard workaround: the meta-test enforcing the `ir` row's `omit` status now subtracts this lane's `sources`, so either spelling would pass it. `commonIr` camel-cases the exact type a rule author has to look up to read the block (`zzop_core::CommonIr`, field list in docs/modules/facade.md) and stays greppable inside a consumer's own codebase, which a two-letter key that is a substring of `circular`/`directory`/`require` is not. The cost is one mapping to remember, because a direct zzop-facade embedding spells the same block `ir` — stated in the `ir` row below so a reader diffing the two surfaces meets it there.
zzop facts.noMcpTwinBecause: (1) The output is deliberately UNCAPPED and grows with tree size, while every MCP reply this repo ships is cap-governed (crates/summary/src/output) — the same argument the `ir` row already makes for the analyze reply, only stronger: `ir` alone measured 107x the shipped reply on zzop's own tree and `facts` carries the whole join on top. The main MCP consumer is an AI agent, so output size is a direct context cost. (2) The consumer is a PROGRAM, not a conversation: the workflow is `zzop facts ./api ./web > facts.json && ./my-rule facts.json`, a terminal/CI act. (3) An agent already has the shaped answers it usually wants (join buckets, check_endpoint); `facts` exists for the case those cannot serve, which is precisely the case that is not a conversation. An agent that genuinely wants it can shell out to the same binary for the identical answer.

reads: trees[].output.ir.symbols + trees[].output.ir.dep (structural membership; non-empty dep source entries additionally feed the per-extension inDepGraph count)
zzop_engine::rule_sightlines (compiled-in per-rule sightline declarations — CAPABILITY input, code not run)
zzop coverage.emits: the aggregate-visibility view: per-extension dispatch table (structural/lexicalOnly/degraded, plus inDepGraph — files of the extension with at least one resolved outgoing dep edge, the per-extension import-resolution sparsity baseline), per-tree blindSpots (class-aware cross of each declared rule sightline with the tree's structural extensions) with blindSpotBasis (what the cross was computed from) and the top-level blindSpotMeaning legend, per-tree warnings forwarded verbatim, the census with joinVisibility spelled as a sentence (naming that only an io-fact-contributing overlay restores join visibility), a conditional walkNote when files under a .git/ segment were walked (the otherTrees convention: absent means none were), and the unmeasured axes as a FIELD — by ruling (2026-07-31) no single score exists in the schema
zzop coverage.noMcpTwinBecause: an authoring/ops aggregate over the whole tree. The MCP agent surface already carries the per-file half (check_file) and the per-run census rides every analyze reply; an agent wanting the aggregate can ask analyze_repo and read coverage. If agent demand for the AGGREGATE arrives, promote then — the core (zzop_facade::query_coverage_json) is host-neutral by construction, so the twin is a dispatch entry away.

reads: nothing from a run — the bundled DSL pack data compiled INTO the binary
zzop explain.emits: One rule's compiled-in data as human-readable lines, or a guided Err naming what the id actually is (a native analysis id, a pack id, an output field id, an ambiguous bare id, or unknown).
zzop explain.noMcpTwinBecause: It answers from data that is already ON the MCP wire as a whole: the `rule-catalog` contract resource carries every shipped rule id with its prose, so an agent looks a rule up by reading one document rather than by calling a tool per id. The subcommand exists because a TERMINAL user wants one rule, not the catalog. Declared here — even though its projection lives in crates/facade rather than crates/summary — because the one-audience fact is what both consumers of this block need: crates/engine/tests/rule_contracts/host_vocabulary.rs's contract 16 subtracts these files when it checks that shared crates name no CLI-only vocabulary, and naming `zzop explain` inside the `zzop explain` lane is correct, not a leak. NOT declared, deliberately: `zzop init`. Its only implementation is the argv entry point (packages/cli-bin/src/cli/run.rs), which this block's `_doc` forbids declaring, and the bytes it writes are a two-audience contract resource that MCP `resources/read` serves as well.

cache.note: Internal engine cache-hit/miss diagnostic (CacheStatsView). Not referenced anywhere in the scanned delivery lane (all three directories — see `_doc`). Available only via the raw zzop-facade output (direct engine embedding) — a deliberate internal-only performance diagnostic, not part of any curated summary.

critical.note: Only the top 3 paths (the engine's own SIZE-WEIGHTED blast-radius ranking: blast_radius * ln(loc+2), with blast radius as the tie-break — crates/metrics/src/criticality.rs::compute_criticality) ride the compact `architecture.criticalTop` summary (crates/summary/src/analyze/shape.rs::architecture_summary). This row said 'blast-radius ranking' until 2026-07-31, which invited a consumer to reproduce the three paths by sorting `critical` on `blastRadius`; that sort is a DIFFERENT order whenever two hubs of similar blast differ in size. The full CriticalFile list (with contributing metrics, in this same order) is available only via the raw zzop-facade output (direct engine embedding).

degraded.note: The raw degraded-path list is capped (DEFAULT_DEGRADED_LIMIT=50) with an explicit `degradedTruncated` disclosure when capped (crates/summary/src/analyze/shape.rs) — `coverage.degraded` already carries the full uncapped count. The full uncapped per-file list is available only via the raw zzop-facade output (direct engine embedding).

disclosure.note: Carried as a FOLD since 2026-07-29 (crates/summary/src/output/disclosure.rs): the reply gets the registry's counts plus a pointer (`zzop contract disclosure-classes` / `zzop://contract/disclosure-classes`), never the ~10.6KB of run-invariant prose. The full text is available from the contract lane on both surfaces and, verbatim, from the CLI-only `zzop facts` lane.

findings.note: Shaped via output::shape_findings into {total, bySeverity, byRule, shown (severity-desc, capped at DEFAULT_FINDINGS_LIMIT=50 unless the caller supplies `limit`), truncated?} — never the raw findings array verbatim.

folders.note: FolderAggregates is never referenced anywhere in the scanned delivery lane (all three directories — see `_doc`) — no folder-level rollup rides the reply. Available only via the raw zzop-facade output (direct engine embedding); unlike nodes/health/recommendations/critical, folders gets not even a compact summary cameo.

gitWindow.note: Forwarded verbatim via a `.get()`-defensive check, only when the key is present (crates/summary/src/analyze/mod.rs) — the facade itself always serializes this field (null when git did not run), but the forwarding step is conditional on presence rather than being an unconditional index. The always-present field is available via the raw zzop-facade output (direct engine embedding).

health.note: Only `health.pain` (the scalar) rides `architecture.pain`; `contributors` (the per-metric breakdown) never reaches the reply. Gated on `health` being non-null (git signals ran this tree). The full health object is available only via the raw zzop-facade output (direct engine embedding).

ir.note: The full CommonIr (dep graph, per-file tags/loc/symbols, and `ir.io`'s provide/consume lists) never rides any MCP/`zzop-mcp` reply. The reason is UNBOUNDEDNESS, not bulk: `ir` grows in proportion to tree size while the shipped reply is capped (findings <= DEFAULT_FINDINGS_LIMIT and friends), so which one is bigger depends entirely on the tree — measured, `ir` is 0.68x the shipped reply on a 52-file tree and 107x on zzop's own. An earlier wording here read 'deliberate token-shaping decision', which invited the false gloss that `ir` is always too large; the honest statement is that a capped reply stays predictable for an agent's context budget and an uncapped `ir` does not. An AI consumer gets the io facts it usually wants through the cross-layer join buckets / check_endpoint instead of the raw `ir` block. AVAILABILITY (changed 2026-07-26 — this row is `omit` for the MCP reply only, it is no longer 'MCP-omitted therefore embed-only'): the CLI-only `zzop facts` lane emits the WHOLE block verbatim, under the key `trees[].commonIr` — same data, different spelling, deliberately (see `_cliOnlyLanes` for the lane, its no-MCP-twin judgment, and the naming rationale); the CLI-only `zzop manifest` lane reads `ir.io.provides` alone and projects it to identity rows — kind/key/source, never the file/line/symbol/body detail; and a direct zzop-facade embedding still yields it under its own `ir` key.

layerCoChurn.note: Never referenced anywhere in the scanned delivery lane (all three directories — see `_doc`). Available only via the raw zzop-facade output (direct engine embedding).

nodes.note: The FileNode list is never forwarded (`architecture.criticalTop` derives from `critical`, a separately-ranked view, not from `nodes`). The full per-file node list (tagCounts, loc, every metric) is available only via the raw zzop-facade output (direct engine embedding).

recommendations.note: Only recommendations[0] (the top ROI-ranked entry) rides `architecture.topRecommendation` ({id, severity, topItem}) — remaining recommendations and each one's full items list are available only via the raw zzop-facade output (direct engine embedding).

ruleOverridesApplied.note: The one CONDITIONALLY-PRESENT top-level field: the facade omits the key entirely (never an empty object) when the caller requested no `disabledRules`/`severityOverrides` — see `zzop_engine::RuleOverridesApplied`'s own doc and crates/facade/src/analyze_tests.rs's `analyze_json_omits_rule_overrides_applied_when_nothing_was_requested`. When present it is forwarded WHOLE and uncapped (bounded by the caller's own request size, same as packsLoaded) through a `.get()`-gated `summary.insert` in crates/summary/src/analyze/mod.rs — the gate is what preserves the omission instead of turning it into JSON `null`. `cross_repo` carries it too, inside each `sources[]` row (see multiAnalyzeOutputView.trees's note). Row added 2026-07-26: this field had NO row here until then, because the single pinned key-set fixture surface_parity.rs reads never requested an override, so the completeness test could not see the field at all; crates/facade/src/analyze_tests.rs now carries a second pin with an override requested, and surface_parity.rs unions the two.

ruleTimings.note: Per-rule performance-timing diagnostic, never referenced in the scanned delivery lane (all three directories — see `_doc`). Available only via the raw zzop-facade output (direct engine embedding) — not meant for a curated AI-consumer or human-facing summary.

scores.note: The raw per-metric Scores struct (which feeds health/recommendations) is never forwarded directly — only the DERIVED `health.pain` and top `recommendations[0]` reach the reply via the architecture summary. Raw scores available only via the raw zzop-facade output (direct engine embedding).

seams.note: SeamCandidate list never referenced in the scanned delivery lane (all three directories — see `_doc`). Available only via the raw zzop-facade output (direct engine embedding).

trees.note: cross_repo reshapes each tree entry into a compact `sources[]` row ({sourceId, path, fileCount, findingCount, packsLoaded, warnings, coverage, ruleOverridesApplied?}) — the raw per-tree AnalyzeOutputView (nodes/scores/health/critical/ir/...) is never forwarded whole; see analyzeOutputView's own rows for what any one nested field gets on its own. The raw per-tree output is available via the raw zzop-facade output (direct engine embedding).

crossLayer.note: cross_repo shapes crossLayer into bucket ROW counts (`buckets.*` — one row per recorded call site), capped edges (`edges`, DEFAULT_EDGES_LIMIT=200, with `edgesTruncated` disclosure), and UNCAPPED DEDUPED bucket keys (`distinctBucketKeys`/`distinctBucketKeyFirstSites` — every distinct key, no truncation field; the 20-key DEFAULT_BUCKET_KEYS_LIMIT and its `bucketKeysTruncated` disclosure were deleted 2026-07-29) — never the raw CrossLayerResult object verbatim. The two views count DIFFERENT things, so `buckets.X >= len(distinctBucketKeys.X)` (measured on cases/: unprovidedConsumes 23 rows / 14 keys, edges 18 / 11), and the reply carries a run-invariant `bucketMeaning` sentence stating exactly that — the arithmetic is answered on the wire, not left to a reader who diffs the two numbers and finds nothing that explains them. Renamed 2026-07-31 from `bucketKeys`/`bucketKeySites` (pre-1.0 breaking rename, same precedent as census `sourceFiles` -> `parserDispatched`): a wire field's NAME must state its membership rule, and the old sites field was plural while carrying only the FIRST site per key. The raw edges/unprovidedConsumes/unconsumedProvides/unresolvedConsumes/externalConsumes/ambiguousConsumes buckets are available via the raw zzop-facade output (direct engine embedding) and, since 2026-07-26, VERBATIM AND UNCAPPED from the CLI-only `zzop facts` lane — plus as UNCAPPED IDENTITY (kind/key/bucket/source, no file or line) from the CLI-only `zzop manifest` lane (both in `_cliOnlyLanes`). The edges cap is why the manifest lane still exists: above it, two runs' replies agree on the edge COUNTS while neither can say which route left the join. Bucket MEMBERSHIP no longer needs that lane.

crossLayerFindings.note: Shaped via output::shape_findings identically to per-tree findings (total/bySeverity/byRule/shown+truncated) — never the raw array verbatim.

warnings.note: ALWAYS written to `summary.warnings`, empty array included (`crates/summary/src/cross.rs`) — the same always-present contract the per-tree warnings/configWarnings fields already had. It was presence-gated until 2026-07-31, which made "this run self-reported nothing" and "this build has no run-level warning channel" the same bytes; the `.get()` on the SOURCE field stays defensive about older engine output, and its absence yields `[]` rather than a judgment. History: this row was the registry's first catch — when first authored, no delivery surface read the run-level field at all (the parallel-implementation-tripwire self-report was silently dropped), the exact shape this registry exists to prevent.

disclosure.note: Carried as a FOLD since 2026-07-29 (crates/summary/src/output/disclosure.rs): the reply gets the registry's counts plus a pointer (`zzop contract disclosure-classes` / `zzop://contract/disclosure-classes`), never the ~10.6KB of run-invariant prose. The full text is available from the contract lane on both surfaces and, verbatim, from the CLI-only `zzop facts` lane.
